transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 14:30 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Dylan Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (BrightCart Lead Engineer), Tom Alvarez (BrightCart PM), Priya Nair (BrightCart Security), Jason (BrightCart SRE)
Links shared: repo: https://github.com/brightcart/pilot-proto, bench sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/brightcart-pilot-bench, redwood snippet deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/pilot-sdk-snippet.pdf

Summary: quick retro on integration week focused on function/tool calling and structured JSON output. We reviewed a few regressions BrightCart saw when optional fields are absent, discussed SDK validation hooks, and next steps for a short perf test that exercises prefix/KV caching and batch sizing. Security/ops follow-up to confirm KMS and VPC microsegmentation for the dedicated option.

Topics: SDK usage patterns, function calling failure modes, structured output schema enforcement, prefix/KV cache behavior, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, compliance (KMS/SOC2), next steps and artifacts.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Laura (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, then Dylan will walk through the edge cases you sent overnight.
[00:12] Maya (BrightCart): Yep hi, Maya here. We got a couple of outputs that were kinda malformed when the catalog items had missing price_meta, so that's what we flagged.
[00:21] Tom (BrightCart): Tom here, and yeah the primary thing is the front-end throws when expected fields are null, so we need the model output to be stricter or the SDK to shield us.
[00:30] Dylan (Redwood SE): Cool, I pulled three of your failing traces from the sheet, thanks for dumping those. I can repro the optional-field drop where the function-calling path returns an empty object rather than the structured array you defined. Quick note: sometimes the parser on our side maps unknown tokens to empty strings, so that might look like a missing key in the transcript.
[00:52] Maya (BrightCart): Huh, ok that might be where our front end misinterprets. But on our side the call to redwoodClient.callFunction('normalizeItem') returned a body with key names but values as "-" in some cases, looks like filler from transcription?
[01:10] Laura (Redwood AE): That dash filler sounds like tokenization fallback; Dylan, is there a guard in the SDK to validate against a JSON schema before it returns to the app?
[01:20] Dylan (Redwood SE): There's a minimal check currently. We do a try/catch around the function payload and attempt a JSON parse, but we don't validate required fields unless you opt into the strict schema flag. We can ship a snippet that shows strictSchema: true which will surface the exact missing fields with a clear error.
[01:38] Tom (BrightCart): That'd be perfect. Our PMs prefer the SDK to fail fast with a line like "missing field price.amount" rather than downstream NPEs.
[01:47] Maya (BrightCart): Also a note, some of the examples call the function via the Node SDK but our pipeline is primarily Python; the behavior between the SDKs looked slightly different in the logs.
[01:58] Dylan (Redwood SE): Hmm, that's interesting. We recently changed the Node streaming layer to normalize trailing commas which may change a couple edge semantics. I'll include both Node and Python snippets.
[02:12] Priya (BrightCart): Quick sec — from security perspective we need to know whether those function payloads ever persist in logs or if they go through KMS for encryption at rest. We can't accept cleartext PII in the hosted logs.
[02:25] Laura (Redwood AE): Great question. We have controls: hosted does redact PII by default for the standard plan and logs are encrypted with customer-specific keys on Dedicated/Private (KMS/HSM). But we should share the SOC2/Type II attestation and a short note on what gets persisted in the console. I'll drop that in the repo.
[02:40] Priya (BrightCart): Please do. Also can you confirm SSO/SCIM support for account provisioning?
[02:47] Laura (Redwood AE): Yes, SAML and SCIM available; I'll attach the SSO guide.
[02:52] Jason (BrightCart SRE): From an ops angle, we want to measure cold-start latency when we have function calling + structured output enforced. If strict schema causes retries or extra parsing that could be a latency hit.
[03:05] Dylan (Redwood SE): Reasonable — I prepared a quick perf plan: small 1000 req sample that toggles strict schema on/off, then vary batch sizes 1, 4, 8. We can also test prefix cache hit scenarios by sending repeated item lookups. That should show token-level latency and throughput differences.
[03:24] Maya (BrightCart): Awesome. Also, one of our engineers noted the KV cache seemed to flush when the session token changed. Is that expected?
[03:33] Dylan (Redwood SE): If you're using ephemeral sessions and not pinning the conversation ID, the KV cache is per pinned session. Session token rotation will invalidate that cache. You can opt into prefix caching at the SDK layer to persist commons across sessions, but you need to manage keys. I'll include sample code.
[03:51] Tom (BrightCart): For the pilot, what's the recommended mode — start hosted and then move to Dedicated only if cost grows, or do Dedicated from day one because of the expected traffic?
[04:05] Laura (Redwood AE): Most customers start hosted to iterate, then provision Dedicated for predictable peak throughput. Given you have PII concerns, Dedicated or Private with customer KMS could be cleaner. We can give you an estimated cost delta; Dylan will calculate the typical per-token/throughput delta for your workload.
[04:22] Priya (BrightCart): We won't commit to Private yet, but if Dedicated gives KMS + audit logs that may be sufficient.
[04:30] Dylan (Redwood SE): Quick aside on quantization: if you go Dedicated we can enable a quantized variant of the model that keeps latency but reduces GPU memory. It can change some token-level probabilities so you should run the eval set.
[04:45] Maya (BrightCart): Noted — we'll run the eval set. On the structured output side, the main pain is partial arrays: sometimes model returns [null, {item}] and our deserializer chokes. Can SDK help normalize nulls to omitted elements?
[04:59] Dylan (Redwood SE): We can provide a normalization hook. But that risks masking upstream problems; better to flag them and have a fallback serializer in the app that prunes nulls. We'll include both patterns in the snippets.
[05:15] Tom (BrightCart): Another real-world gotcha: our business logic expects a stable key order because we do a shallow compare for caching. Random key ordering breaks it. Any chance Redwood can guarantee key ordering in structured payloads?
[05:29] Dylan (Redwood SE): JSON object ordering is not guaranteed, but if you request an array-of-tuples or a canonicalized string via the SDK we can return stable order. We'll show that in the code.
[05:42] Maya (BrightCart): Good. Also, one of the traces included a fallback to the 'small' model when capacity was constrained and the output schema changed — that surprised us.
[05:52] Laura (Redwood AE): That's the smart routing behavior — automatic fallback can return a different model variant. You can pin model versions per-route to avoid that. There's also a routing policy to prefer latency or cost; we'll help you set the route for the checkout flow to pin to the higher quality model.
[06:08] Priya (BrightCart): For audit we'll need change logs for model rollouts. Is there a history API?
[06:14] Dylan (Redwood SE): Yes, the console exposes rollout history and per-model diffs; we can add a note about retention windows and exportability.
[06:23] Jason (SRE): For the perf tests, can we run them from our infra into your hosted endpoint to capture realistic network latency?
[06:31] Laura (Redwood AE): Absolutely. We'll give a temporary key with limited scope. After the perf test, we'll rotate it.
[06:38] Maya (BrightCart): Quick question about the function call signatures — what's best practice for errors? Our front end needs error codes to render different UI states.
[06:47] Dylan (Redwood SE): We recommend a small envelope: {status: OK|ERROR, code: string, payload: {}}. Use codes like RATE_LIMIT, VALIDATION_ERROR, etc. The SDK will translate common infra errors to those codes if you enable normalizedErrors: true.
[07:09] Tom (BrightCart): Can you also include a tooling hook for local dev? Our devs want to run the same function-calling behavior locally without hitting the cloud for every iteration.
[07:20] Dylan (Redwood SE): We have a dev proxy that stubs the function runtime; it sits behind the SDK and can be toggled with REDWOOD_LOCAL_DEV=true. I'll add setup steps in the repo.
[07:33] Maya (BrightCart): Great, that'll speed things up.
[07:36] Laura (Redwood AE): Let's recap next steps then action items.
[07:40] Dylan (Redwood SE): Quick technical note — the failing traces you shared had one which looked like a streaming truncation; transcript shows "...price meta" then the stream ended. For long responses consider using streaming + resume tokens so the client can recover partials.
[07:59] Maya (BrightCart): I remember that one — it was during a high-latency window. We'll try streaming.
[08:06] Tom (BrightCart): Ok, schedule wise, we'll aim to run the validation harness by Friday and reconvene early next week if needed.
[08:13] Laura (Redwood AE): Sounds good. I'll upload the SDK snippets and SOC2 + SSO guides today, Dylan will send the perf plan and KV cache notes by Thursday.
[08:24] Priya (BrightCart): Thanks, that'll help for our compliance sign-off.
[08:29] Laura (Redwood AE): Any final questions?
[08:32] Jason (BrightCart SRE): None from me.
[08:34] Maya (BrightCart): No, thanks.
[08:36] Tom (BrightCart): Thanks everyone.
[08:38] Laura (Redwood AE): Thanks all, we'll follow up in the sheet and with PRs.

End of transcript.
